column3: Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “have I taken” for ox and donkey and has no separate “Tell me” before the promise to restore.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew does not repeat Samuel’s name and uses a singular verb for the final response; BSB has “they replied”.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly repeats the LORD’s name in “the righteous acts of the LORD”; BSB uses “He”.
The Hebrew repeats the LORD as the sender and does not explicitly say the messengers were sent “to them”.
The Hebrew repeats singular “hand” with each of the three oppressors; BSB combines the last two and uses plural “hands”.
The Hebrew has singular “hand”; BSB uses plural “hands”.
The Hebrew has singular “hand”; BSB uses plural “hands”.
The Hebrew says “a king shall reign over us” without an explicit “we must have”.
The Hebrew explicitly repeats the relative “whom”; BSB varies the second reference as “the one”.
The Hebrew retains the image of the LORD’s mouth and has no separate phrase “then all will be well”.
The Hebrew says “against you and against your fathers”; BSB makes the second phrase a comparison with the past.
The Hebrew describes the LORD as doing this great thing with a participle; BSB uses a future “will do”.
The Hebrew calls the thunder “voices” and says the evil was done “in the eyes of the LORD”; BSB uses “thunder” and “in the sight”.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names “all the people” as speakers; BSB uses “they”.
The Hebrew explicitly names both Samuel and the people he addresses; BSB omits the audience noun.
The Hebrew repeats the word for emptiness; BSB varies it as “worthless things” and “empty”.
The Hebrew repeats the LORD’s name and explicitly says He made them a people for Himself; BSB uses “He” and “make you His own”.
The Hebrew says he will teach them without a separate “continue”.
The Hebrew says “only” and imperatively “see”; BSB has “Above all” and “consider”.
The Hebrew emphasizes doing evil by repeating its root; BSB expresses this as persisting in evil.
